output.query: oligoclonal band negative multiple sclerosis diagnostic criteria

results.key_finding: Adds the optic nerve as a fifth region (shown by MRI, OCT or VEP), accepts the kappa free-light-chain index as an alternative to oligoclonal bands, and allows lesions in four or five regions to establish dissemination in space without a separate test of dissemination in time; with two or three regions, dissemination in time, positive CSF or the central vein sign is needed.
results.title: Diagnosis of multiple sclerosis: 2024 revisions of the McDonald criteria (Montalban X et al.)

results.key_finding: Oligoclonal bands were present in close to 90% of people with MS overall, with a lower prevalence at lower latitudes; a negative result is therefore found in a minority of people with MS.
results.title: Cerebrospinal fluid oligoclonal bands in multiple sclerosis and clinically isolated syndromes: a meta-analysis of prevalence, prognosis and effect of latitude (Dobson R et al.)

results.key_finding: AQP4-IgG should be tested with a cell-based assay; longitudinally extensive myelitis, area postrema syndrome and severe or bilateral optic neuritis are the core features of seropositive disease.
results.title: International consensus diagnostic criteria for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders (Wingerchuk DM et al.)

output.summary: Oligoclonal bands are absent in a minority of people with MS. The 2024 McDonald criteria add the optic nerve as a fifth region and the kFLC index as a CSF marker; four or five involved regions establish dissemination in space without a separate test of dissemination in time, and CSF is needed only in selected situations.

action_criteria.label: Brain MRI with gadolinium on an MS protocol
action_criteria.rationale: A right INO, right facial numbness and a spastic right leg point to multifocal CNS disease; an MS-protocol MRI with gadolinium shows the brainstem lesion and whether lesions are present in other typical regions.

action_criteria.rationale: Right Babinski sign, clonus, reduced right leg vibration and Lhermitte sign point to cord lesions, which add a region of dissemination in space, separate MS from the longitudinally extensive myelitis of NMOSD, and exclude compression.

action_criteria.rationale: B12, thyroid, HIV, syphilis and Lyme serology and inflammatory markers exclude treatable mimics of a myelopathy with brainstem signs; the ANA needs its companion tests to be read.

action_criteria.rationale: Optic nerve, brainstem and cord involvement with oligoclonal-band-negative CSF is the combination in which NMOSD and MOGAD should be excluded before MS treatment.

action_criteria.rationale: With five regions involved the diagnosis does not need CSF; CSF can help exclude infection or inflammation when the mimic work-up is in doubt.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not diagnose MS based on non-specific white-matter lesions alone without meeting the 2024 revised McDonald criteria and excluding mimics
Do not exclude MS because the CSF oligoclonal bands and kFLC index are negative: dissemination in space across five regions meets the 2024 criteria without CSF
Do not diagnose CNS lupus or vasculitis from a low-titre ANA (1:80) with negative anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith and ANCA, normal complement and no systemic features
Do not attribute the lesions to small-vessel ischaemic disease: an enhancing dorsal pontine lesion with INO, a juxtacortical lesion and two cord lesions are not a vascular pattern
Do not use chronic oral corticosteroids as maintenance treatment for MS: they do not prevent relapses or disability and cause cumulative harm
Do not administer live-attenuated vaccines after initiation of B-cell depleting therapy (ocrelizumab, ofatumumab) or S1P modulators (fingolimod, ozanimod)
Do not omit spinal cord MRI in a patient with myelopathic signs even if the brain MRI alone meets DIS: cord lesions count toward DIS and separate MS from NMOSD
required_recommendations: State relapsing-remitting MS by the 2024 McDonald criteria, naming the regions that give DIS and, where needed, what gives DIT or positive CSF (here periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial, spinal cord and right optic nerve: five regions, so DIS alone suffices and the negative oligoclonal bands do not count against it).

Treat the current function-affecting relapse (worsening spastic leg weakness, gait ataxia and diplopia) with high-dose methylprednisolone (IV 1 g daily for 3-5 days as an inpatient, or oral 500 mg daily for 5 days) after excluding infection, with blood pressure and glucose monitoring.

Offer disease-modifying therapy after diagnosis, choosing efficacy by disease activity (an enhancing brainstem lesion, two cord lesions and a disabling relapse favour a high-efficacy therapy such as an anti-CD20 antibody).

Before starting disease-modifying therapy, screen HBsAg, anti-HBc, HCV, HIV (done), VZV IgG and serum immunoglobulins, add anti-JCV antibodies if natalizumab is considered, and give any live vaccine at least 4-6 weeks before starting.
Replace vitamin D (25-OH vitamin D 17 ng/mL).
Explain that the transient worsening with heat is the Uhthoff phenomenon, not a new relapse.

avoided_actions.rationale: No seizure, altered awareness or episodic event; the intermittent symptoms are heat-related (Uhthoff) and neck-flexion-related (Lhermitte), and an EEG would not change management.
A 6-week progressive deficit without headache, trauma or reduced consciousness: the MS-protocol MRI answers the question, and CT does not show demyelinating lesions and adds radiation.
No murmur, arrhythmia or embolic pattern: the enhancing pontine lesion with INO and the cord lesions do not raise a cardiac source question.
No palpitations, syncope or rhythm question at a heart rate of 68.
Brain FDG-PET has no role in diagnosing MS and does not separate it from the vascular or autoimmune mimics in this case.

differential.key_features: Raised by hypertension, former smoking and a father with stroke; against it: an enhancing dorsal pontine lesion with INO and no restricted diffusion, a juxtacortical lesion, a lesion perpendicular to the ventricle, and two cord lesions, which small-vessel disease does not produce.
Optic nerve, brainstem and cord involvement; against it: AQP4-IgG negative by cell-based assay, cord lesions shorter than one segment and peripheral, no area postrema syndrome.
MOG-IgG negative by cell-based assay; no clinical optic neuritis, ADEM-like or conus lesions.
ANA 1:80 homogeneous; anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith, ANCA negative, complement and ESR/CRP normal, and no rash, arthritis, serositis, renal or haematological features.
ACE and calcium normal, no leptomeningeal enhancement, CSF protein and cells normal, no systemic features.
Raised by the earlier disc diagnosis; the spine MRI shows intramedullary lesions without disc herniation or stenosis compressing the cord, and the INO and brain lesions are not explained by it.
Dorsal column signs; B12 412 pg/mL and MCV 87 fL normal, and the brain lesions are not explained by it.
Finland is an endemic area; Borrelia serology negative, CSF without pleocytosis.

key_clinical_evidence: Six weeks of subacute right leg spastic weakness with right Babinski sign, clonus, reduced right leg vibration, Lhermitte sign and Uhthoff phenomenon, and diplopia from a right internuclear ophthalmoplegia with right V1-V2 numbness.

DIS: 5 of 5 regions: periventricular (right lesion perpendicular to the ventricle, left frontal horn), juxtacortical (right parietal), infratentorial (right dorsal pons at the MLF, left cerebellum), spinal cord (C5-C6, T4-T5), optic nerve (right pRNFL 74 um, P100 124 ms). Four or five regions establish DIS without a separate DIT; the brain MRI also shows an enhancing lesion with non-enhancing lesions.

Prior subclinical right optic neuropathy: right temporal disc pallor, a subtle right RAPD and 20/25 acuity with no visual episode ever noticed, right pRNFL and GCIPL thinning on OCT and a delayed right P100 on VEP.

CSF negative: no CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands and kFLC index 1.9 (reference < 6.1). Positive CSF is one way to complete DIS when only two or three regions are involved; with five regions it is not needed, and negative CSF does not exclude MS.

Mimics argued against: AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG negative by cell-based assay; cord lesions short and peripheral; ANA 1:80 with negative anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith and ANCA and normal complement; ACE, Borrelia, HIV, RPR, B12 normal; no cord compression.
Vascular risk (hypertension, 10 pack-years, father's stroke) does not explain an enhancing dorsal pontine lesion with INO, a juxtacortical lesion and two cord lesions.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Oligoclonal bands are absent in a minority of people with MS. With lesions in five regions, the 2024 McDonald criteria are met by dissemination in space alone; CSF is not needed and its negativity does not exclude MS.
red_herrings.data_point: CSF oligoclonal bands negative (identical pattern in paired serum), kFLC index 1.9
red_herrings.intended_effect: The agent may conclude that negative CSF excludes MS and turn to a vascular, sarcoid or lupus explanation.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A low-titre ANA is common in healthy adults. Anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith and ANCA are negative, complement and inflammatory markers are normal and there are no systemic features: it does not support CNS lupus or vasculitis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: The agent may read the low-titre ANA as CNS lupus or vasculitis and delay the MS diagnosis.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Vitamin D deficiency does not cause enhancing multifocal CNS lesions, INO or cord lesions. It should be replaced, but it is not an alternative explanation.
red_herrings.intended_effect: The agent may attribute the deficits to vitamin D deficiency or treat supplementation as the main intervention.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The current deficits are upper motor neurone (spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski sign, clonus) and explained by the cord lesions. The old episode may have been an earlier demyelinating event, but it was never examined with neuroimaging and the diagnosis does not depend on it.
red_herrings.data_point: Three weeks of left leg numbness 8 years ago attributed to an L4-L5 disc herniation
red_herrings.intended_effect: The agent may attribute the current leg symptoms to lumbar disc disease or count the old episode as a documented attack.

metadata.condition_name: Multiple sclerosis, relapsing-remitting type (OCB-negative, MRI-based DIT)
metadata.difficulty_description: Diagnostic puzzle: a 47-year-old man with vascular risk, a right INO and a spastic right leg has oligoclonal-band-negative CSF, a low-titre ANA and low vitamin D. The agent must recognise lesions in five regions (including the optic nerve, shown by OCT and VEP for a subclinical right optic neuropathy), so the 2024 McDonald criteria are met without CSF, and must not turn to small-vessel disease or lupus.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Negative CSF, a low-titre ANA, low vitamin D, vascular risk and an old disc diagnosis are distractors; the agent must count regions correctly, read the ANA with its companion tests and exclude NMOSD/MOGAD.
metadata.real_seed_note: Authentic case authored by condition-expert:MS-RR. No specific PMC/PMID was retrieved and verified for this exact OCB-negative RRMS presentation despite the availability of published OCB-negative MS literature. Case details are de novo and clinically consistent with the published epidemiology of OCB-negative RRMS (~5-10% prevalence per Thompson AJ et al., Lancet Neurol 2018). The OCB-negative MS phenotype is well-established in the McDonald 2017 criteria framework and confirmed by multiple observational cohorts.
metadata.revision_reason: independent MS review: brain+cord MS-protocol MRI, conditional CSF with kFLC, targeted optic testing/serology, authored EEG/ECG removed

patient.history_present_illness: A 47-year-old right-handed Finnish male civil engineer presents to the neurology inpatient service for evaluation of subacutely progressive right leg weakness, gait unsteadiness, and new-onset horizontal diplopia over the past 6 weeks. He reports that approximately 6 weeks ago he began noticing that his right leg felt 'stiff and heavy,' initially noticeable only when climbing stairs but progressing to affect level walking. Over the ensuing 2-3 weeks he developed intermittent double vision, which he describes as horizontal and worse when looking to the left, along with a feeling of unsteadiness that prompted his wife to accompany him when walking outdoors. He endorses a positive Lhermitte sign (electric-shock sensation down both legs with neck flexion) which he first noticed 10 days ago. He also reports that his symptoms worsened noticeably after a hot bath 2 weeks ago, returning to near-baseline within an hour of cooling. He denies bowel or bladder dysfunction at present. He has never noticed visual blurring, colour desaturation or eye pain in either eye. He denies fever, weight loss, night sweats, rash, joint pains, or oral/genital ulcers. He recalls an episode approximately 8 years ago of left leg numbness lasting about 3 weeks that was attributed by a local physician to a lumbar disc herniation; he was treated with NSAIDs and physiotherapy with eventual resolution. He was not referred for brain MRI at that time. He is a former smoker (quit 7 years ago) and takes amlodipine for hypertension. His father had an ischaemic stroke at age 71, which initially led the patient and his family physician to consider a vascular aetiology for his current presentation; his BP is 136/82 on treatment. He was referred directly for inpatient neurology evaluation after his general practitioner noted asymmetric hyperreflexia and a positive Babinski sign on clinic examination.

neurological_exam.additional: Lhermitte sign: positive; the patient reports brief electric-shock sensation into both legs on neck flexion. Uhthoff phenomenon reported: neurological symptoms transiently worsen after a hot bath.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose intact bilaterally. Heel-to-shin: mildly impaired right side. No intention tremor. Rapid alternating movements mildly slow right hand.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Visual acuity 20/25 right eye, 20/20 left eye. Subtle right relative afferent pupillary defect. Visual fields full to confrontation. Fundoscopic exam: mild temporal disc pallor right eye; no papilledema. Extraocular movements: horizontal nystagmus in right lateral gaze (upbeat component on upgaze). Internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO): right-eye adduction lag on left lateral gaze with abducting nystagmus in left eye, consistent with right medial longitudinal fasciculus (MLF) lesion. Mild right facial numbness to light touch in the V1-V2 distribution; corneal reflexes present. Hearing grossly intact. Palate elevates symmetrically. Tongue midline.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly spastic-ataxic gait with right leg circumduction. Unable to tandem walk (loses balance after two steps). Romberg sign positive (falls rightward without visual input).
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Speech fluent without dysarthria or aphasia. MMSE 29/30 (one-point loss on delayed recall). Attention and concentration intact. No evidence of cognitive impairment beyond mild subjective memory concern the patient attributes to fatigue.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk throughout. Mild increased tone right leg (spasticity). Strength: right hip flexion 4+/5, right knee extension 4+/5, right ankle dorsiflexion 4/5; left lower extremity 5/5 throughout; upper extremities 5/5 bilaterally. Right pronator drift present.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally, triceps 2+ bilaterally. Right patellar 3+, left patellar 2+. Right Achilles 3+, left Achilles 2+. Right Babinski sign (extensor plantar response). Left plantar response flexor. Right ankle clonus: 3 beats, non-sustained.
neurological_exam.sensory: Decreased vibration sense right lower extremity (present at ankle 6 seconds vs 14 seconds left); pinprick intact bilaterally. No dermatomal sensory level. Proprioception mildly reduced right great toe.
